title: The trombone's role in the band
summary: Playing between melody and harmony, figurations and rhythm parts.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Yeah, and go around, see? Is there anything you can tell about the style the trombone should play in a band that is more of a... I know some of this myself. I mean, I know how you play and how they sound. Yeah, sure. But anything that you could say here on the record, like whether it should be more of a bass part, or if they do pretty, they play cello parts. Yeah. Should it be more of a rhythm? Yeah. Or what kind of a melody?

Well, it depends on how the melody runs. If you've got a good stomp melody, you know, or something like that, trombone should be played right between the melody and the other part of the harmony, like the after beats and the after counts and all that. And you use, you might say, well, you might say a whole note. Use a whole note in some places, you know, see? And then use, play a figurations, you know, a figurations around, playing those figurations around on a melody when a fellow's playing. And don't stay in your part all the time. Jump in the lead somewhere else. Don't stay there long, though, because you're taking his part from him. Play hitting the lead sometime and get away from there and going back to vamping and bass. And that's the reason I could balance, make a, I could balance any orchestra. I could put any orchestra on good balance because that's the way I play with him, see? I'll play the lead around when the fellow thinks I'm moving my ducks away from him and go over here. I could hear it on the rest. See, you can hear it on the things. Duck away from him and go over there somewhere.
Is there a trombone that can play either melody or sort of like a rhythm part, too, at times?

Yeah, rhythm is. With little sharks to play, like you say, snap it off. Yeah, it snaps off, see? That's the peggos and things like that in the part. It's nice if you can handle them, see? A lot of fellas try to handle them and they get some mixed up, see? And it slows them down, see? It slows them down. You can't get those notes in between those peggos, you know? And that kind of slows them down. That's what makes them scared to take venture out, you know, to try to do anything. If you can play a peggos and you're, you know, with that peggos, you play it in and then jump into the melody. But some fellas, when they're doing that, making a peggos, they make it so slow, they can't get that up note, you know? They can't get that turn note, see? There's turns, you know, see? Like that. It's easy, all right.
